properties.description: Hold inviolable intent (KPPs) and COMPUTE when the design breaks one. BUILT 2026-07-25. Anthony's call on shape: a discriminated Constraint (`category: kpp`) rather than a new node type, because the quantity/limit/direction triple and the budget rollup are exactly what a KPP needs and already existed unused — and because an enum value plus a property is upgrade-SAFE where a new node type would refuse older binaries, which mattered on a day that already shipped two edge-type changes. Added `objective` beside the existing `limit`, giving the acquisition pair: threshold is the minimum acceptable, objective is what success looks like. Objective is optional and never invented, because a number the graph asserts on its own is the one thing intent vocabulary must not do. THREE VIOLATIONS, ranked ABOVE ordinary gaps because a breached KPP is not thinness in the design, it is the design failing. UNBOUND (0.90) — a KPP constraining nothing can never be violated, so it sits permanently green while asserting something vital; the quietest failure and the reason 'a KPP that nothing checks is a comment'. Reported once, not three times: an unbound KPP cannot also be breached or contradicted, and counting one fault three ways would teach people the findings are noise. BREACHED (0.95) — the budget rollup crossed the threshold, reusing budget_report wholesale. The only arithmetic violation, and the reason a KPP is worth distinguishing from a requirement nobody adds up. An INCOMPLETE rollup is deliberately NOT a breach: asserting failure from absent data is the silent guess this project forbids. CONTRADICTED (0.85) — an ACCEPTED decision governs what the KPP binds, surfaced for review and explicitly not asserted as a violation, since whether it truly costs the KPP is semantic. Proposed decisions are excluded: an open choice has traded nothing away, and flagging it would punish thinking out loud. 9 tests. FOUND WHILE BUILDING: GOVERNED_BY runs FROM the governed node TO the Decision, so the first implementation walked it backwards and found nothing — caught by the test rather than by review. THE CAPTURE HALF IS cap:kpp-proposal AND IS NOT BUILT: this computes violations of KPPs that exist; it does not notice that a stated need SHOULD be one.
properties.name: Hold inviolable intent (KPPs) and compute when the design breaks one
